QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_43

question.text: The Treynor Ratio of a fund is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.9.2: Treynor Ratio = (Rp − Rf) / β. It measures excess return per unit of SYSTEMATIC (non-diversifiable) risk, as captured by portfolio beta. The Trap: Option A is the Sharpe Ratio (uses standard deviation, not beta). Options B and C are malformed and do not represent any standard risk-adjusted return metric. Note: Treynor is most meaningful for well-diversified portfolios; for undiversified or concentrated AIF portfolios, Sharpe is more informative because it captures total risk rather than only systematic risk.
